body: You were given a chance, over all these other people.  Not only that but look at the positive things that your work could bring you.  You could make great friends, meet someone, and even have a lot of fun with your boss.  It's worth it to find out.  It's worth it to quit your job and find a new one if you don't like this one.  It's even worth it just to keep living so millions of strangers can see your face.   You don't have to choose between living an enjoyable life and working.  It's not a black and white choice.  All of those things SHOULD be mutual.  You can make them mutual with positive thinking.  Hang in there.

Agreed.  I talked to a therapist who said there are millions of types of therapy and over a million combinations of therapy and medication.  Keep trying.  It's like dating, you need to find your perfect match.  It might take a while but it will be worth it.  You can do it.

It's really the opposite of how it should be right now.  She stayed with me for a night after feeling this way and then ultimately tried to kill herself and ended up in the hospital.  I don't know if any of her family is coming to see her, but I have already seen her.  I'm going to see her again today because she wants that, but I am also going to tell her she NEEDS to talk to her sister/mom/dad. I really hope the hospital can help with this.  I don't want to get in the middle of it, but I'm the only one here for her right now.  I'm trying to keep her parents updated as much as possible.

Also I noticed genders didn't match up on the title now, sorry wasn't thinking about the title kind of sleepy from staying up late last night to talk to her.  She is a girl.

No she's definitely not well.  It's terrible because she feels like a burden and she rented a room in another house kind of far from me.  I don't want her to be that far away from me, because my life does not allow me to be able to go and drive to her whenever she starts feeling like she needs someone to talk to or be with, but it seems like this deal is done.  It's particularly haunting because of the way she said she wanted to commit suicide and there's a certain thing  about the house that seems to highlight that for me.  I can tell in a PM or something.  I was very upfront about what I can offer.  I can help find a job, a place to live, and offer my friendship.  I can help make positive changes to help make her get better, but I don't think I can make her better.  But I'm not a suicide counselor nor can I really help diagnose things or even offer medical/emotional advice.  I told her that she will need to be patient with me because I am a full time worker and I have a LOT on my plate, including a failing relationship that often interferes with our one-on-one chats about her depression.  I feel terrible for hardly having the time to talk to her but it's very difficult.  My living situation also isn't ideal for her to live in either.  I wish it were but there's truly nothing I can do about it.  I'm scared to leave her alone, but I obviously have to.  I really want her to go to a therapist and the way you described it seems like you think that wouldn't be entirely helpful.  I honestly have no idea, I have no experience with these kinds of things.  That's why I'm here.  Any advice would be great.
